topics.title: Pressure in Fluids
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand that pressure is the result of a force applied over an area (u, s)
understand the effect of depth on the pressure in a fluid and the implications of this (u, s)
understand the nature of the atmosphere and how atmospheric pressure is measured (u, s)

body.text: Pressure is the force acting on each unit of area. For the same force, a smaller area produces a bigger pressure — this is why a drawing pin has a sharp point, and why a tractor's wide tyres spread its weight to avoid sinking into soft ground.

In a fluid (a liquid or a gas), pressure increases with depth: the deeper you go, the greater the weight of fluid pressing down from above. This is why a dam wall is built thicker at the bottom than at the top, and why the pressure at the bottom of the sea is much higher than at the surface.

The atmosphere is the layer of air surrounding the Earth. Air has weight, so it exerts pressure — atmospheric pressure — which can be measured with a barometer. Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, which is why it becomes harder to breathe high up a mountain.
